query: Consider the following context: High entropy alloys have excellent wear resistance, so they have great application prospects in the fields of wear resistance and surface protection. In that context, which material can be used for adhere to the surface of a Cu matrix, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A coating made of an FCC-structured high entropy alloy such as equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi will adhere well to a copper matrix and enhance its wear resistance due to its intrinsic high hardness and fine nanostructured precipitates that promote load transfer at the interface.
generation.material_initial_state: A copper substrate (matrix) with its typical ductile, low-hardness microstructure.
generation.intervention: Deposit a thin film or coating of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high entropy alloy onto the copper surface via a process such as magnetron sputtering or thermal spraying.
generation.conditions: Standard coating conditions at room temperature (or moderately elevated temperatures) where the copper substrate is not degraded, with subsequent room temperature or moderate annealing to enhance interfacial bonding.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a graded interfacial region with interdiffusion between copper and the HEA; the presence of nanoscale Mn- or Cr-rich precipitates that can act as anchoring points to improve adhesion.
generation.mechanism: The HEA coating exhibits high wear resistance due to its high hardness and the possible simultaneous presence of nano‐sized precipitates (e.g., Mn2O3 in similar systems) that provide Orowan strengthening. Furthermore, its multi-element composition can favor interfacial diffusion, leading to an adherence layer that bridges the distinct lattice structures (FCC Cu and FCC HEA).
generation.predicted_outcome: The copper composite with the HEA coating is expected to show significantly enhanced surface hardness and wear resistance compared to uncoated copper, with a stable interfacial bond that resists delamination under mechanical stress.
generation.baseline: Bare copper exhibits low hardness and poor wear resistance, leading to rapid surface degradation in abrasive or high-contact environments.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis is expected to hold as long as the processing route maintains a controlled interdiffusion zone without forming brittle intermetallic phases and the thermal expansion mismatch between copper and the HEA remains minimal under the operating temperature range.
generation.uncertainty: Exact interfacial chemistry and long-term durability under cyclic mechanical and thermal stresses are uncertain and require further experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare copper samples with and without the deposited equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA coating using controlled magnetron sputtering. Subject both sets to standardized wear tests (e.g., pin-on-disk) and adhesion tests (e.g., scratch testing) under identical conditions.
measurements: Surface hardness using micro- or nanoindentation
Wear rate quantification under abrasive conditions
Interfacial adhesion strength assessed by scratch tests and cross-sectional microscopy
Interdiffusion layer thickness measured by TEM/EDS
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the HEA-coated copper does not exhibit a statistically significant improvement in wear resistance and interfacial adhesion (e.g., less than 20% improvement compared to uncoated copper) or if brittle intermetallic phases develop at the interface leading to premature coating delamination, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

System: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy (HEA). Processing: Selective laser melting (SLM) using pre-alloyed spherical powder (average diameter 27.2 µm); laser power 90 W, scan speed 600 mm/s, hatch space 80 µm, layer thickness 25 µm, volumetric energy density 75 J/mm³, 180° rotation scanning pattern, high-purity Ar atmosphere.. Test conditions: Compression tests at 25, 500, 600, 700, 800, and 900 °C; initial strain rate 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹; engineering strain limit 0.4; specimens preheated at 10 °C/min; MoS₂ lubricant used..
